lesson.title: It Is Needed
lesson.subtitle: il faut + infinitive (il faut partir, il faut voir) and il me faut + noun.

hook.title: il faut: Obligation and Need Without Pointing a Finger
hook.content: Followed by an infinitive, il faut expresses obligation (Il faut confirmer 'We/you need to confirm'). Followed by a noun and paired with me, te, nous, vous, il me faut means 'I need [something]': Il me faut un billet ('I need a ticket'), Qu'est-ce qu'il vous faut ? ('What do you need?')!

footnotes.title: How 'Il me faut du temps' and 'J'ai besoin de temps' are sister ways to say 'I need time'
footnotes.content: French gives you two everyday ways to say 'I need X': J'ai besoin de X and Il me faut X!

pattern.title: Il faut + Infinitive ('Must do'); Il me/te/vous faut + Noun ('Need [a thing]')
pattern.content: Practice both patterns and negate them with Il ne faut pas.
pattern.linguist_note: Dative experiencer + impersonal falloir (Il me faut un livre) parallels dative-need constructions across Romance.
pattern.trap_note: Remember: Il ne faut pas partir means 'You/we MUST NOT leave' (prohibition)!

exercises.prompt: Match each il faut expression with its natural English translation:
exercises.target_answer: We / you must reserve, We / you must not forget, I need a coffee, We need two tickets, What do you need?
exercises.meaning: Il faut réserver, Il ne faut pas oublier, Il me faut un café, Il nous faut deux billets, Qu'est-ce qu'il vous faut ?
exercises.explanation: me, te, nous, vous before faut tell who needs the item.

exercises.prompt: What is the literal word-for-word structure of 'Il nous faut deux tables'?
exercises.meaning: Literal structure: It to-us is-needed two tables

exercises.prompt: A baker asks you 'Qu'est-ce qu'il vous faut ?' How do you answer 'I need some bread' using 'faut'?
exercises.explanation: Keep impersonal Il at the start and place me before faut: Il me faut du pain.

exercises.idea: we need to confirm the reservation today (using Il faut)
cues: It is needed to confirm → Il faut confirmer
the reservation today → la réservation aujourd'hui
exercises.target_answer: Il faut confirmer la réservation aujourd'hui
exercises.meaning: We/you need to confirm the reservation today

diagnosis.cue: faut only ever takes impersonal Il: Il faut confirmer.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Il me faut dix minutes pour finir
exercises.target_answer: Il me faut dix minutes pour finir
exercises.meaning: I need ten minutes to finish
exercises.explanation: Il me faut dix minutes + pour finir ('in order to finish').
exercises.affirmation: You paired Il me faut with pour finir cleanly.

summary.outcome: Use il faut + infinitive for obligations and il me/te/nous/vous faut + noun for 'needing things'.

use_example.german: Qu'est-ce qu'il te faut ? — Il me faut mon billet.
use_example.english: What do you need? — I need my ticket.

summary.takeaway: Il faut + verb = 'must [verb]'; Il me faut + noun = 'I need [noun]'.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([2702] The Subjunctive Door): see how It Is Needed leads directly into The Subjunctive Door.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "We/you need to confirm the reservation today" in French:
twist.target_answer: Il faut confirmer la réservation aujourd'hui
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Il faut confirmer la réservation aujourd'hui" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of It Is Needed.

faut.english_meaning: is necessary (il faut: one must / it is needed)
faut.context_translation: We/you have to leave now (lit. It is necessary to leave).
faut.etymology_derivation: From Latin fallere 'to be lacking' — what is lacking is what is needed! Only ever used with il.

me.etymology_derivation: Elides to m' before a vowel: il m'écoute.

te.etymology_derivation: Elides to t' before a vowel: je t'aime.

nous.etymology_derivation: Latin nōs — English keeps the root in nostrum.

vous.etymology_derivation: Latin vōs 'you all' promoted to politeness — the same T–V ladder as German Sie and English's lost 'ye'.

aller.context_translation: I'm going to go to the café.
aller.etymology_derivation: Latin ambulāre 'to walk' → ambler → aller. To go is a stroll away — and the near future rides on it.

venir.etymology_derivation: Prefix it to build a whole family: revenir (come back), devenir (become), prévenir (warn).

confirmer.etymology_derivation: confirmation → confirmer. Strip -ation, bolt on -er (pronounced /e/), and the noun becomes the verb.

billet.etymology_derivation: Double ll after i sounds like /j/.

pain.etymology_derivation: Latin pānis 'bread' — a pantry is literally the bread-room. The N is thought, not said: the nasal vowel is the lesson.
